quirks.description: push() and reclaim() do not check that the connection is checked out: one handed back twice is idle twice, so count() exceeds the size and destroying both copies drives the reserved capacity below zero.
quirks.case: scenarios.json#a connection reclaimed twice is idle twice, and the count goes past the size

deviations.php: The Swoole channel holds `size` connections: pushing one more (a connection handed back twice) blocks the coroutine until another is popped, a deadlock when nothing will.
deviations.reason: The Rust Channel adapter grows instead of blocking a task forever; handing a connection back twice is a caller bug either way, and the Stack adapter (which PHP lets grow too) has a pinned case.

deviations.php: Observable gauge callbacks hold the pool, so a pool bound to telemetry lives as long as the telemetry adapter and keeps reporting.
deviations.reason: Rust callbacks hold the pool weakly: a dropped pool frees its resources and stops reporting, which no case can observe from PHP without leaking it.

deviations.php: An adapter's synchronized() can throw (a subclass failing to lock), and the pool then forgets the connection (PoolTestScope::testUseForgetsConnectionWhenDestroyCleanupFails).
deviations.reason: The Rust pool keeps its bookkeeping under its own lock, which cannot fail: the failing-lock fixture (`arm`) does nothing in Rust, and the case shows the same outcome (a fresh resource on the next use).

deviations.php: release() can be overridden by a subclass to throw, and Group::use() still releases every other connection and rethrows the first failure (GroupTestScope::testGroupUseReleasesEveryConnectionWhenCleanupThrows).
deviations.reason: Pool is not subclassable in Rust and its release cannot fail, so there is no cleanup failure to propagate; the case is replaced by one where the callback throws.

deviations.php: A group holds pools of any resources, and use() hands their resources to a variadic callback.
deviations.reason: A Rust Group holds pools of one resource type and adapter (use an enum resource for mixed pools); with() hands the callback a Vec.
